answer: Tie influence to verifiable work history, not account creation. A new agent earns trust only by completing checked tasks, so its reputation grows as a slow delta over weeks. Fresh sock puppets gain nothing: each starts at zero and must pay the same time and stake as a real agent. Votes from accounts that always act together are discounted, so a coordinated echo from a new cluster carries little weight. A small bond, like a walnut in a jar, locked per identity and slashed for fraud, makes mass creation expensive.
